PullRequest.Title: eslint: fix bracket notation in test infrastructure
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- replace identifier-safe bracket notation with dot notation across the 18 files in the **Test infrastructure** exclusion group
- remove the completed group from `.eslint-allowed-bracket-notation-files`

This is a mechanical cleanup for `local/code-no-bracket-notation-for-identifiers` with no intended behavior changes.

## Validation

- targeted ESLint across all 18 affected files
- targeted hygiene across all 18 affected files
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run transpile-client`
- compiled smoke tests and automation infrastructure
- compiled sanity tests with their locked TypeScript version
- typechecked the component-fixture Playwright project with its locked TypeScript version
- syntax-checked the affected JavaScript runners with `node --check`
- component-fixture Playwright: 4 passing resize-observer scenarios
- focused core unit tests: 11 passing accessibility service tests, exercising the shared instantiation mock and Electron unit-test bootstrap

## Stacking

Stacked on #334756 and intended to merge after that PR.

Scenarios.Scenario: Component-fixture chat resize, ResizeObserver warning capture, and Playwright geometry assertions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Fixture rendering and resize callbacks still perform the same style write, widget layout, dataset reads/writes, and getBoundingClientRect calls before each test assertion can complete. The diff only changes bracket access with a literal identifier to equivalent dot access.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: DOM style/layout updates and geometry reads in the browser fixture
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One unchanged layout per fixture resize callback and two unchanged geometry reads per Playwright assertion; dataset access cardinality is also unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same DOM properties and dataset keys were accessed through bracket notation, with identical callbacks and boundary-call count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing layout and geometry operations remain on the fixture-test critical path, but the diff adds no operation or forced-layout transition.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of fixture resize/error events and test scenarios; no change to effective event or DOM-operation cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Resize callbacks and browser-page evaluations remain scheduled exactly as before; no queue, batching, or parallelism change.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is read or modified. Dataset key identity and browser behavior are unchanged for cold and repeated fixture runs.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that there is no changed performance mechanism because each edit addresses the same object and exact same property key without moving or duplicating work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser property-access micro-cost can vary by engine, but bracket access using a constant identifier and dot access have no material scaling or boundary difference here.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: synchronous layout-sensitive work is pre-existing and unchanged in frequency, ordering, and resource use.

Scenarios.Scenario: Multi-diff fixture serialized-state import and geometry-oscillation parsing
Scenarios.CriticalPath: JSON parsing and per-item validation must complete before the fixture state can render. Changed accesses read the exact same identifier-named fields from the same parsed objects.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Parse and validate serialized fixture JSON items and geometry settings
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One unchanged field-validation pass per imported fixture item and optional geometry object.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same fields were read once using constant-string bracket notation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Validation remains on fixture import's critical path; the diff neither adds another pass nor changes per-item work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Imported fixture item count and optional geometry fields; effective O(items) validation is unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Parsing is synchronous and serial before and after the diff; no concurrency mechanism is changed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or coalescing is involved; each explicitly imported state is parsed once as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from direct before/after equivalence and unchanged parser control flow.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material: JavaScript dot access and constant identifier bracket access target the same keys and do not alter collection traversal.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: serialization CPU and allocation behavior are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Automation and smoke-test UI polling for SCM actions, search tooltip, and settings layout
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing automation polling/renderer communication must observe matching DOM snapshots before tests proceed. Only reads such as attributes.title and attributes.style changed syntax.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Automation waits for renderer DOM elements and snapshots through the existing test driver
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The same wait operation and predicate evaluation count per test; no extra polling request or element traversal is introduced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Predicates and returned values accessed the identical title/style keys with bracket notation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing waits remain test-critical, but predicates read the same keys and therefore do not alter polling or IPC cardinality.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of polling retries and matching elements; neither is changed by the property-access substitution.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing awaited waits remain serial in each test and test-runner parallelism is untouched.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache, invalidation, or negative-cache behavior; automation snapshots are consumed as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from unchanged selectors, awaits, predicates, and exact property keys.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual retry counts depend on UI timing, but the diff cannot increase them through a performance mechanism because predicate semantics are identical.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: no added polling, IPC, traversal, or synchronous UI work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Sanity, smoke, ESM, and Electron test startup/configuration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Environment/options resolution, remote test-directory creation, local server/browser or Electron launch, and crash-reporter setup occur before the respective test suites run. The changed accesses resolve the same environment variables, CLI options, and Playwright export.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create the remote test data directory recursively
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one existing mkdirSync for a configured user-data directory per resolved launch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same directory was created before assigning the same environment keys via brackets.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Remains synchronous on remote test setup's critical path; the diff only changes subsequent environment-object assignment syntax.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One unchanged browser launch per runner invocation in the shown paths; smoke and Electron runner selection is unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same Playwright browser object, environment variables, and minimist options were selected through bracket notation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Browser/process startup remains on suite startup's critical path, with the same executable selection and launch options.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start and use the existing local ESM-check server before browser launch
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One unchanged local server startup per ESM-check run.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Server startup and sequencing were identical; only playwright['chromium'] became playwright.chromium.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing server startup precedes browser launch; no network work was added or moved.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of test-runner invocations, configured launches, and environment reads; each remains constant per invocation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Startup awaits and launches preserve existing serialization; no limiter, queue, or fan-out is modified.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm/cold node_modules, browser binaries, and filesystem state may affect startup duration, but cache keys and access patterns are untouched.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence because all expensive calls and awaits are unchanged and only equivalent property syntax differs.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Underlying launch and filesystem durations vary by host, but their count and critical-path placement are demonstrably unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: subprocess, filesystem, network, and startup work is unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Instantiation service mock reuse and Electron unit-test preload/renderer initialization
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Unit tests inspect mock metadata to decide whether to reuse a service, then initialize preload cwd handling, crash reporting, and renderer inspection defaults. Each changed access addresses the same property.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create or reuse Sinon mocks/stubs for requested test services
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One unchanged metadata check per service request; mock/stub creation is still skipped or performed under the same conditions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: sinonOptions metadata was read and assigned under the same key via bracket notation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Mock setup remains on individual unit-test setup paths, with no additional creation or lookup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Electron preload/renderer bridge and process initialization for unit tests
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One unchanged initialization sequence per Electron test renderer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same VSCODE_CWD and util.inspect.defaultOptions values were accessed through bracket notation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initialization remains startup-critical, but no bridge call or process operation is introduced.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of requested mock services and Electron test renderer starts; lookup and initialization cardinality are unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Instantiation remains synchronous and Electron initialization ordering is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: ServiceCollection reuse behavior is identical because sinonOptions key identity is unchanged; no cache lifetime or invalidation changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from exact property-key equivalence and unchanged branches.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Sinon service creation cost varies by test, but the reuse branch condition is semantically identical.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: mock reuse, allocations, and Electron setup work remain unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 19 changed files and every diff page. The PR replaces constant-string bracket notation with equivalent dot notation for identifier-safe keys and removes the corresponding lint exclusions. Hot resize/layout paths, parser loops, automation polling, mock creation, and test startup boundaries retain identical control flow, cardinality, concurrency, and lifecycle; no actionable diff-introduced performance regression or concrete regression fix was found.
